ontario-social-studies-g4-all-strands.documentTitle: Ontario Social Studies Grade 4 - Overall Expectations
ontario-social-studies-g4-all-strands.documentVersion: Ontario Social Studies, History, and Geography Curriculum (2026)

standards.unit: Heritage and Identity: Early Societies to 1500 CE
standards.strand: Heritage and Identity: Early Societies to 1500 CE
standards.summaryText: compare key aspects of life in a few early societies (to 1500), including at least one First Nation and one Inuit society, each from a different region and era and representing a different culture, and describe some key similarities and differences between these early societies and present-day Canadian society
standards.officialOutcomeText: compare key aspects of life in a few early societies (to 1500), including at least one First Nation and one Inuit society, each from a different region and era and representing a different culture, and describe some key similarities and differences between these early societies and present-day Canadian society
standards.curriculumFocus: Heritage and Identity: Early Societies to 1500 CE

standards.unit: Heritage and Identity: Early Societies to 1500 CE
standards.strand: Heritage and Identity: Early Societies to 1500 CE
standards.summaryText: use the social studies inquiry process to investigate ways of life and relationships with the environment in a few early societies (to 1500), including at least one First Nation and one Inuit society, with an emphasis on aspects of the interrelationship between the environment and life in those societies
standards.officialOutcomeText: use the social studies inquiry process to investigate ways of life and relationships with the environment in a few early societies (to 1500), including at least one First Nation and one Inuit society, with an emphasis on aspects of the interrelationship between the environment and life in those societies
standards.curriculumFocus: Heritage and Identity: Early Societies to 1500 CE

standards.unit: Heritage and Identity: Early Societies to 1500 CE
standards.strand: Heritage and Identity: Early Societies to 1500 CE
standards.summaryText: demonstrate an understanding of key aspects of a few early societies (to 1500), including at least one First Nation and one Inuit society, each from a different region and era and representing a different culture, with reference to their political and social organization, daily life, and relationships with the environment and with each other
standards.officialOutcomeText: demonstrate an understanding of key aspects of a few early societies (to 1500), including at least one First Nation and one Inuit society, each from a different region and era and representing a different culture, with reference to their political and social organization, daily life, and relationships with the environment and with each other
standards.curriculumFocus: Heritage and Identity: Early Societies to 1500 CE

standards.unit: People and Environments: Political and Physical Regions of Canada
standards.strand: People and Environments: Political and Physical Regions of Canada
standards.summaryText: assess some key ways in which industrial development and the natural environment affect each other in two or more political and/or physical regions of Canada
standards.officialOutcomeText: assess some key ways in which industrial development and the natural environment affect each other in two or more political and/or physical regions of Canada
standards.curriculumFocus: People and Environments: Political and Physical Regions of Canada

standards.unit: People and Environments: Political and Physical Regions of Canada
standards.strand: People and Environments: Political and Physical Regions of Canada
standards.summaryText: use the social studies inquiry process to investigate some issues and challenges associated with balancing human needs/wants and activities with environmental stewardship in one or more of the political and/or physical regions of Canada
standards.officialOutcomeText: use the social studies inquiry process to investigate some issues and challenges associated with balancing human needs/wants and activities with environmental stewardship in one or more of the political and/or physical regions of Canada
standards.curriculumFocus: People and Environments: Political and Physical Regions of Canada

standards.unit: People and Environments: Political and Physical Regions of Canada
standards.strand: People and Environments: Political and Physical Regions of Canada
standards.summaryText: identify Canada’s political and physical regions, and describe their main characteristics and some significant activities that take place in them
standards.officialOutcomeText: identify Canada’s political and physical regions, and describe their main characteristics and some significant activities that take place in them
standards.curriculumFocus: People and Environments: Political and Physical Regions of Canada
